Fetch all analyses for a study, choose the columns you need, and save the table
to your computer. Edit and run the cells in order.

## Choose a study

Replace `STUDY` with another MGnify study accession to download its analyses.

```{pyodide}
import requests
import pandas as pd

API = "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metagenomics/api/v2"
STUDY = "MGYS00010393"
```

## Collect the analyses

The API returns results in pages. Collect each page, then flatten the nested
sample and assembly records into dataframe columns.

```{pyodide}
records = []
page = 1
while True:
    response = requests.get(
        f"{API}/studies/{STUDY}/analyses/",
        params={"page": page, "page_size": 1000},
        timeout=30,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    batch = response.json()
    records.extend(batch["items"])
    if not batch["items"] or len(records) >= batch["count"]:
        break
    page += 1

analyses = pd.json_normalize(records)
print(f"Fetched {len(analyses)} analyses")
analyses.head()
```

## Choose columns and download

Edit the column list below, or use `selected = analyses` to keep every column.
You can also filter rows before exporting. Run this cell again after making changes
to update the download.

```{pyodide}
#| define: [csv_text, csv_filename]
selected = analyses.reindex(columns=[
    "accession", "experiment_type", "pipeline_version",
    "sample.accession", "assembly.accession",
])
csv_text = selected.to_csv(index=False)
csv_filename = f"{STUDY}-analyses.csv"
selected.head()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
DOM.download(new Blob([csv_text], {type: "text/csv;charset=utf-8"}), csv_filename, "Download CSV")
```

The CSV contains the selected rows and columns.

## Running this code in your own environment

Install the packages from a terminal:

```bash
python -m pip install pandas requests
```

Run the Python cells in a notebook or script. Save the selected dataframe with
`selected.to_csv("analyses.csv", index=False)`.
